name: set_limit_field_to_1500
description: Stores the constant 1500 in a 16-bit field at offset 30 of the object passed in the address register and returns.

name: update_object_state_machine
description: Copies a position field into a saved field, then picks a timer from a flag byte in the linked record. It either sets the pending flag or dispatches to the handler selected by the state index in the jump table.

name: set_pending_flag_minus_20
description: Stores minus 20 in the field at offset 132 of the object and sets bit 5 of its flags word.

name: advance_countdown_and_dispatch
description: Sets the state to 14 and, while the position differs from the saved one, counts the countdown down. When the countdown reaches zero it clears the pending values and dispatches through the state table; otherwise it stores 20 as the pending value and sets the pending flag.

name: set_pending_flag_plus_20
description: Stores 20 in the field at offset 132 of the object and sets bit 5 of its flags word.

name: process_idle_timer_state
description: If the linked record has a blocking flag or a nonzero counter, it sets the limit field to 1500 and exits. Otherwise it sets state 4 with a six-frame timer and counts the timer down, and when the position matches it compares a helper value against 600 and 29.

name: run_six_frame_countdown_state
description: Sets state 4 and a timer of 6, then counts the timer down. On reaching zero it switches to state 5 and dispatches; when the position already matches, it compares a helper value against 600 and 29 and clears the timer.

name: check_helper_value_limits
description: Calls a helper and, if its value exceeds 600, clears the timer field and sets the limit field to 1500. If the value exceeds 29 and a second helper value falls outside plus or minus 32, it clears the timer field.

name: clear_countdown_field
description: Clears the 16-bit countdown field at offset 26 of the object.

name: clear_countdown_and_set_limit
description: Clears the countdown field at offset 26 and sets the limit field at offset 30 to 1500.

name: dispatch_state_handler_five
description: Sets the state field to 5, calls two helpers to select the object pointer, then invokes the handler found in the state table at the index held in that object.

name: read_flagged_table_value
description: When bit 10 of the object's flags is set, reads a value from a linked table entry and returns it if the entry's count is positive. Otherwise it clears bit 0 of the entry and returns zero; with bit 10 clear it returns the masked flags.

name: select_next_table_entry
description: Clears bit 0 of the linked record and calls a helper. If the record's type is 7 and the state is not 5, it sets pending flags and returns -1; otherwise it copies the record's state and link pointers, decrements the entry count and returns the index scaled by 4.

name: copy_template_block_and_reset
description: Copies a block of 36 longwords from a fixed source area to a fixed destination area, calls a helper, then writes four fixed globals to their initial values.

name: tick_global_delay_or_pick_state
description: Counts down a global delay and returns the stored value while it is nonzero. Once the delay expires, it returns the masked low bits, or when a specific code is reached it picks a new state from a lookup table indexed by a helper result.

name: return_masked_table_flags
description: Stores the input index in a global and returns the flags of the matching table entry masked to bits 11 and 13. The decompiler marks an unimplemented instruction on the zero path, so that path is not recovered.

name: search_record_table_for_match
description: Searches a table of 38-byte records for an entry whose fields match the current object, wrapping around the table. When bit 10 is set it returns a value from a linked list instead. The end of the routine is cut off by unimplemented instructions.

name: decrement_counter_restore_state
description: Decrements the countdown at offset 120. While it stays nonzero it sets a global to 255 when the countdown is below 5; at zero it copies the saved state at offset 66 into the state field.

name: restore_saved_state
description: Copies the saved value at offset 66 of the object into its state field at offset 42.

name: clamp_offset_toward_target
description: When bit 3 of the object's flags is set, moves the field at offset 16 toward a target derived from a stored value and a linked field, limiting each step to plus or minus 20, and sets a global flag.

name: dispatch_sequence_word_advance
description: Reads the next command word from the object's sequence pointer and calls the routine selected by that word. The pointer advances by one word unless the command was zero.

name: advance_animation_step_on_timer
description: Counts the timer at offset 126 down. When it expires, it steps a global index capped at 3 and loads the frame number, two table values and flag bits for that step, then sets offset 30 to 5372.

name: step_animation_index_and_load
description: Increments a global animation index capped at 3, then loads the frame number, two table values and flag bits for that index into the object and sets offset 30 to 5372.

name: check_window_and_arm_timer
description: Clears the countdown at offset 26, then checks that a helper value lies between minus 100 and 100. If it does and a second helper value is below 31, it clears the countdown and returns minus one; otherwise it sets the countdown to 40 and returns zero.

name: steer_offset_toward_target
description: Stores two helper results and returns zero when the first value lies outside minus 100 to 100. Otherwise it sets a countdown of 25 and, when bit 3 is set and the second value is below 201, moves the field at offset 16 toward a target by at most 20.

name: return_flag_if_helper_zero
description: Calls a helper routine and returns minus one when its result is zero, otherwise zero.

name: compute_scaled_globals_or_default
description: If a global is set and not equal to 512, it derives two global values by scaling other global coordinate values. Otherwise it sets both of them to 127.

name: sync_indexed_values_call_helpers
description: Compares two indexed global values with their stored copies. Where one differs, it saves the new value and calls helper routines, either a pair repeated twice or a series of eight helper calls.

name: wrapped_difference_call_return_value
description: Calls a helper, then takes the difference between a global value and a register value wrapped into a 168-unit cycle. When the wrapped difference lies within plus or minus 22, it calls two helpers and returns the register result of the second.

name: call_helpers_within_wrapped_window
description: Takes the difference between a global value and a register value, wrapped into a 168-unit cycle. When it lies within plus or minus 22, it calls two helper routines.

name: call_helpers_within_wrapped_window
description: Takes the difference between a global value and a register value, wrapped into a 168-unit cycle. When it lies within plus or minus 22, it calls two helper routines.

name: update_cached_byte_value
description: Compares a byte from the current record with a cached copy in the same record. On change it stores the new byte and calls helpers, returning the byte when unchanged, zero when the new byte is zero, and otherwise the helper result.

name: forward_single_helper_call
description: Calls one helper routine and returns, with no logic of its own.

name: reset_four_entries_when_active
description: Loops over four table entries spaced 24 bytes apart and sets the first word of each entry whose field at offset 16 is nonnegative to 5632.

name: sync_record_cache_bytes
description: Walks a table of 24-byte records up to a fixed end address. Where a record's byte at offset 36 differs from its cached copy, it updates the cache and calls a helper.

name: clear_flag_bits_on_four_entries
description: Clears the low three flag bits of byte 8 in four 32-byte entries from a fixed base, then sets bit 3 of the entry selected by a global index.

name: reset_entry_and_indexed_entry
description: Resets the entry at the current index by clearing its low flag bits and setting offset 26 to minus one and offset 30 to 512. It then sets offset 26 to minus one, bit 3 and offset 30 to 256 on the entry given by the input value.

name: refresh_entry_graphics_on_change
description: For each entry, when its stored type byte changes, copies 16 rows of four words each from a lookup table into the entry's display area. It then synchronises two more cached fields and calls helpers.

name: drain_slots_or_subtract_budget
description: If the counter is zero and does not exceed the input, it works out a scaled shortfall and drains four slots by it, then resets the object's position and timer fields to fixed values. Otherwise it subtracts the input from the counter, clamping at zero.

name: drain_slots_and_reset_record
description: Drains a scaled amount across four slots using a register input. If the counter is nonzero, it resets the object's position and timer fields to fixed values and returns a value.

name: distribute_increment_across_active_entries
description: When a global is set, counts the active slots among four 32-byte entries. It then adds an equal share of a shared accumulator, which loses one-sixteenth on each call, to each active slot's value at offset 20, capped at 6144.

name: add_amount_to_active_entries
description: Adds the input amount to the value at offset 20 of each active entry among four 32-byte slots. Active means the global is set or the entry's byte at offset 1 is nonzero, and the sum is capped at 6144.

name: return_global_times_eight
description: Returns the global value shifted left by three bits, which multiplies it by eight.

name: set_global_to_one_if_zero
description: Sets a global flag to one when it is currently zero and leaves it unchanged otherwise.

name: advance_cycling_frame_state
description: Advances a small state machine that cycles a frame index from zero up to a limit and counts a 16-step delay. It moves between its states depending on the counters at the object's offsets 0 and 2.

name: refresh_display_palette_rows
description: Loads five color entries from a lookup table chosen by a global flag, then copies two blocks of 16 rows of four words into the display area. It finally merges a 16-row mask table into the display with AND and OR operations.

name: call_helper_three_times
description: Calls one helper routine three times in succession.

name: call_helper_count_down_loop
description: Calls a helper once for each value of a counter, from its starting value down to zero.

name: trigger_status_and_helper
description: When the global is nonzero, it sets a status value to 255, calls a helper and clears the global. Otherwise it sets an indexed status byte to 255 and calls a helper if that byte was zero. The block that copies a table of globals is unreachable from this flow.

name: lookup_object_and_call_helpers
description: Looks up an object pointer by index and, when the index exceeds 2048 and the object is valid, calls helpers. If the object's type is 2544, it swaps one field with the global value around the helper calls.

name: reset_record_slots_on_change
description: When a per-index byte differs from the current global, it stores the new byte and clears four 12-byte records by setting a byte to 255 and a word to minus one. It then calls a helper.

name: store_value_in_index_table
description: Stores the global value into the word slot of a four-byte-stride lookup table at the index given by the global.

name: select_indexed_table_value
description: Stores the input index in a global, sets the global to the index plus 4 (or plus 12 when that result is 2), then loads the table word stored for the index into the global.

name: set_indexed_byte_ten
description: Writes the constant 10 into a byte of a 12-byte-stride table at the index passed in the data register.

name: set_indexed_byte_five
description: Writes the constant 5 into a byte of a 12-byte-stride table at the index passed in the data register.

name: initialize_indexed_cell_codes
description: Stores the input in a global and writes the constant codes 5 and 10 into a run of globals and into a 12-byte-stride table at the current index. The order of the codes depends on whether the input equals 1.

name: sync_two_record_codes
description: For two 12-byte records, compares a status byte with its per-index copy at the given index. Where they differ, it stores the new value and calls a helper.

name: sync_three_record_codes
description: For three 12-byte records, compares a status byte with its per-index copy at the given index. Where they differ, it stores the new value and calls a helper.

name: fill_cell_strip_threshold_codes
description: When the global exceeds 1024, it fills a strip of 16 four-byte cells with the code 10. It then writes 5 into a cell at a position scaled from the global and writes 6 into the first cells for a count derived from the global, capped at 80. Otherwise it only fills the strip with 10.

name: fill_cell_strip_scaled_codes
description: Fills a strip of 16 four-byte cells with the code 10 and sets one cell at a position scaled from the global value to 5. It then writes 6 into the first cells for a count derived from the global value, capped at 80.

name: set_strip_cell_from_flag
description: Computes a slot index from a helper result, wrapping through 16 slots, then writes a code of 5 or 1 into that slot's four-byte strip cell. The choice depends on a flag byte for the same slot.

name: write_strip_cell_conditional
description: Writes one of two register values into the strip cell for the low four bits of the input. The second value is used when that slot's flag byte is nonzero, otherwise the first.

name: sync_strip_cell_shadow
description: Compares the strip cell for the current slot with its shadow copy. Where they differ, it stores the new value and calls a helper with the value expanded into both bytes of a word.

name: call_helper_sixteen_times
description: Calls a helper routine once, then calls helper routines in a loop of sixteen iterations.

name: clear_four_flag_longwords
description: Sets four consecutive longwords of the flag area to zero.

name: set_flag_byte_from_helper
description: Calls a helper, takes the top four bits of its result as an index, and sets that entry of the flag table to 255.

name: fill_flag_table_minus_one
description: Sets four consecutive longwords of the flag table to minus one, with every bit set.

name: combine_flag_bytes_when_active
description: Combines two flag-table bytes and calls a helper with the result when it is nonzero. The guard tests the same global for contradictory values, so the body is never reached as decompiled.

name: update_slot_timers_and_shares
description: Walks four 12-byte slots, adding the input amount to the active ones and clamping their values between zero and 5632 while tallying totals. It then resets four 32-byte entries with a share of those totals; a final six-longword copy is guarded by a self-comparison and never runs as decompiled.

name: call_six_helpers_undecoded
description: Decompilation timed out, so the body is not recovered. The routine has 43 instructions, is called from two places and calls six other routines, and its purpose cannot be determined from these facts.

name: call_two_helpers_undecoded
description: Decompilation timed out, so the body is not recovered. The routine has 21 instructions, is called from two places and calls two other routines, and its purpose cannot be determined from these facts.

name: dispatch_by_record_type
description: Reads a type byte from the object at offset 94, scales it by eight and calls the handler stored in a jump table for that type.

name: find_entry_and_dispatch
description: Walks a table of three-word entries until a negative marker, matching the object's fields at offsets 12 and 82 against the first two words. On a match it calls the routine selected by the entry's third word, through a jump table the decompiler could not recover.

name: find_entry_and_dispatch_offset
description: Performs the same table search as the neighbouring dispatcher, but adds the matched third word to a base register before the call, so the target is relative to that base.

name: scan_entries_and_dispatch
description: Scans a three-word table from the current position until an entry matches the two input words or a negative marker is reached. It then calls the routine selected by that entry's third word, relative to a base register.

name: call_dispatch_entry_target
description: Calls the routine at the address formed by a base register plus the word at offset 4 of the pointed-to entry.

name: set_global_high_bit
description: Sets bit 15 of the global word and leaves its other bits unchanged.

name: set_global_top_two_bits
description: Sets bits 14 and 15 of the global word and leaves the lower bits unchanged.

name: clear_global_top_two_bits
description: Clears bits 14 and 15 of the global word, keeping the lower 14 bits.

name: sync_four_entry_bytes
description: For four 24-byte entries, compares a byte at offset 20 with its per-slot copy at the global index. Where they differ, it stores the new value and calls a helper.

name: call_helper_per_list_entry
description: Walks a list of words from the pointer stored at offset 18 of the object, calling a helper for each non-negative word, and returns the terminating negative word.

name: push_value_to_small_queue
description: Appends the input word to a three-entry array using the global as the write index, then advances the index. Once the index reaches three it resets the index and clears a byte.

name: clear_three_globals_and_flag
description: Sets three globals and one byte to zero.

name: clear_two_globals_and_flag
description: Sets two globals and one byte to zero.

name: clear_global_after_marking
description: Writes 255 to a global and then zero, leaving the global at zero.

name: copy_record_bytes_or_scale_value
description: When the condition holds, copies three bytes from the record at offset 95 into globals, clears two counters and returns zero. Otherwise it recomputes a scaled value from the record's state and writes constants into the record fields before returning.

name: step_sequence_table_value
description: Counts a global delay down and, when it expires, compares a small run of stored values to pick the next one. It advances an index through a byte table at one of two fixed bases and writes the looked-up value back.

name: check_byte_thirteen_and_scale
description: Clears a global, calls helpers and reads a byte from the pointer passed in. When that byte is 13 it increments the global and multiplies it by 1280; otherwise it calls a helper when the global is below 25.

name: complement_flag_and_run_sequence
description: When the global is zero it complements it. If the result is zero, it calls a helper fifteen times, sets the global to 255 and calls two more helpers; otherwise it clears the global and calls one helper.

name: run_fifteen_calls_then_flag
description: Calls helpers fifteen times in a row, sets a global to 255, and then calls two more helper routines.

name: transfer_half_budget_to_field
description: Reads the object's type word. For most types it moves half of a global budget into the field at offset 136, capped at a limit from a table, and calls a helper when the cap changes the field. For two special types it draws that field into the global budget, up to 192 at a time, and when the field empties it sets the type to 1296 and calls a helper.

name: decay_four_slot_values
description: Reduces the 16-bit value of four slots, spaced 24 bytes apart, by 64 each, stopping at zero.

name: forward_single_helper_call
description: Calls one helper routine and returns, with no logic of its own.

name: run_frame_timers_and_state
description: Decrements several frame timers and, when one expires, relinks a list pointer and calls helpers. It derives a mode code from the state. The decompiled output is truncated partway, so the remaining logic is not recovered.

name: scan_linked_objects_and_dispatch
description: Scans a linked list of objects for entries whose type and state bytes match the global, calling helpers on matches. It then walks an array of 38-byte records, dispatches those matching through a jump table and updates their state bits.

name: test_object_type_flags_noop
description: Tests a flag word and the object's type word, but both branches return immediately, so the routine has no visible effect.

name: test_flags_noop_return
description: Tests a flag word on the object and returns in either case, so the routine has no visible effect.

name: return_flag_status_code
description: If the byte at offset 94 is nonzero, returns minus one when bit 9 of the flags word is clear and zero otherwise. If that byte is zero it returns the input register unchanged.

name: search_linked_records_in_range
description: Returns minus one when the global count is zero. Otherwise it walks a linked structure of records with a stack, calling a helper for each. For records whose value at offset 72 exceeds 19, it compares a scaled offset against a table limit and returns zero within the limit, or minus one when the value exceeds 300.

name: clear_two_globals
description: Sets two globals to zero.

name: scale_global_on_code_thirteen
description: When the input is 13, it clears the global, increments it and multiplies it by 1280. For any other input it calls a helper only when the global is below 25.

name: compute_scaled_index_from_inputs
description: Stores the two register inputs in globals and sets a global to the second input times 1280 plus the first input times four.

name: call_helper_over_null_string
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte string, calling a helper once per character, and returns zero.

name: double_and_accumulate_longword
description: Adds a 32-bit global to itself and to a second 32-bit accumulator, storing the result in the global. The carry is propagated between the 16-bit halves.

name: flag_and_clear_pointed_byte
description: Calls helpers, sets a global to 255, calls another helper, then clears the byte addressed by the pointer.

name: format_digit_or_space
description: Writes one character to the text pointer. For a zero input with the global clear it writes a space and swaps the register halves; otherwise it sets the global to minus one for a nonzero input and writes a digit.

name: call_helper_if_nonnegative
description: Calls one helper routine when the global is zero or positive and returns otherwise.

name: call_helper_if_nonnegative
description: Calls one helper routine when the global is zero or positive and returns otherwise.

name: call_helper_if_nonnegative
description: Calls one helper routine when the global is zero or positive and returns otherwise.

name: call_helper_if_nonnegative
description: Calls one helper routine when the global is zero or positive and returns otherwise.

name: write_three_channel_codes
description: Writes the codes 4, 3 and 5 into three consecutive bytes of the target pointer, calling helpers after each write. It then sets globals to 8, 0 and 255.

name: xor_decode_table_byte
description: Derives a wrapped table index from a helper result and an input word, then returns a table byte XOR-decoded with a key built from another table entry plus 165.

name: xor_decode_offset_table_byte
description: Computes a wrapped table offset from the input word and an index-derived value, then returns a table byte XOR-decoded with a key taken from another table entry plus 165.

name: check_repeat_counter_byte
description: Copies a longword to a stack slot and compares a table byte with a counter byte. On a match it increments the counter, and sets a global to 255 when a flag byte is zero; on a mismatch it resets the counter to zero.

name: compare_repeat_counter_byte
description: Compares the input's low byte with a counter byte. On a match it increments the counter and sets a global to 255 when a flag byte is zero; otherwise it resets the counter to zero and returns the input unchanged.

name: call_eighteen_helpers_undecoded
description: Decompilation timed out, so the body is not recovered. The routine has 118 instructions, is called from one place and calls 18 other routines, and its purpose cannot be determined from these facts.

name: dispatch_table_entry_matching_global
description: If the global is nonzero, scans a table of six-byte entries until a zero key. On a key matching the global it clears the global and calls the handler stored at offset 2 of that entry, through a jump table the decompiler could not recover.

name: clear_global_and_call_handler
description: Clears a global and calls the handler whose address is stored at offset 2 of the pointed-to entry, through a jump table the decompiler could not recover.

name: setup_blitter_rectangle_flags
description: Selects a bit index from a flag word of the object, sorts two coordinate pairs and computes a width and height in 16-pixel units. It then programs the Amiga custom-chip blitter registers, waiting for the blitter to be idle before each write.

name: setup_blitter_rectangle_from_pairs
description: Sorts two coordinate pairs, computes a width and height in 16-pixel units, and programs the Amiga custom-chip blitter registers, waiting for the blitter to be idle before each write.

name: call_helper_until_string_end
description: Repeatedly calls a helper while the byte at the text pointer is nonzero, then returns zero.

name: repeat_helper_until_flag
description: Loops, calling a helper and then a second helper on each pass, and ends when the first helper leaves its flag set.

name: select_buffer_and_copy_block
description: Chooses one of two buffer base addresses from the input and the previous selection, advances it by 4096, then copies 2000 blocks of four longwords from the buffer at the toggled address, offset by 32768. It calls a helper once at the start.

name: unpack_run_length_stream
description: Decodes a packed byte stream into memory. A byte with the high bit clear copies that many literal bytes; with the high bit set it copies a run from an earlier position given by a big-endian word offset. The byte 255 ends decoding.

name: unpack_run_length_variant
description: Decodes the same packed format as its neighbour, with literal runs and back-references, and stops at a 255 marker that is followed by a zero word.

name: unpack_packed_stream_offsets
description: Decodes packed data using the same literal and back-reference format, and returns zero when a zero marker word is followed by a zero byte.

name: call_three_helpers_in_order
description: Calls three helper routines in sequence and returns.

name: call_two_helpers_in_order
description: Calls two helper routines in sequence and returns.

name: copy_table_and_set_words
description: Copies 8001 longwords from one buffer into two destinations and calls helpers. It then stores a computed word value into a set of fixed globals and copies one more value.

name: store_computed_word_table
description: Stores a computed word value into a set of fixed globals and copies one more global from a fixed source.

name: call_three_helpers_in_order
description: Calls three helper routines in sequence and returns.

name: scan_run_bounds_into_record
description: Scans outward in two directions with a helper that returns a status code, stopping at a code other than 2. It stores the resulting bounds and a count into a record and advances the record pointer.

name: emit_scan_span_records
description: Repeatedly scans in two directions with a helper, storing each span as a record, until the lower bound exceeds the upper bound. It then stores the record count and advances the record pointer.

name: clear_scan_state_globals
description: Sets several global scan values to zero. The assignments that copy a global to itself leave that global unchanged.

name: and_three_helper_words_repeated
description: Repeats 512 times: obtains three words from helper routines and stores their bitwise AND at the output pointer.

name: conditional_set_99_and_call
description: When the global is nonnegative, calls a helper, sets the global to 255 and then to 99, and returns the result of a second helper. Otherwise it returns the global unchanged.

name: update_flagged_table_entries
description: Repeats seven times: draws a value from a helper, checks a flag byte in a 48-step table, and where it is set writes a derived byte into a 12-step table. It then copies two bytes from offsets 31 and 25 of the same block into its final cells.

name: initialize_tables_and_defaults
description: Initialises four 24-byte entries, six 12-byte records each set to its index, sixteen four-byte cells, several globals, and four 32-byte entries with fixed bit patterns.

name: copy_negative_status_and_clear
description: Looks up the object for the global index. If its byte at offset 30 is negative, it copies that byte to offset 27, then clears the word at offset 34 and sets the global to 255.

name: call_two_helpers_in_order
description: Calls two helper routines in sequence and returns.

name: wait_helper_until_register_zero
description: Calls one helper, then repeatedly calls a second helper while the data register value it leaves behind is nonzero.

name: call_helpers_with_middle_step
description: Calls two helper routines, then a fixed helper, then three more helper routines, in that order.

name: run_state_loop_with_blitter_wait
description: Saves several globals, waits until the Amiga blitter is no longer busy, then runs a loop that dispatches on a state byte until a terminal code. It finally restores the saved globals.

name: forward_single_helper_call
description: Calls one helper routine and returns, with no logic of its own.

name: add_input_to_global
description: Adds the register input to the global value.

name: call_helper_then_store_routine_address
description: Calls a helper, then stores the address of a routine in a global.

name: call_helpers_when_flag_set
description: When the global is nonzero, calls a helper. It also calls a second helper with the address register when the second register was zero on entry.

name: call_helper_when_global_set
description: Calls one helper routine when the global is nonzero and returns otherwise.

name: update_sound_slots_and_periods
description: Advances eight sound slots, each with a countdown and a state, using a shift-and-XOR generator. It then writes the period registers of the four Amiga audio channels. The decompiled output is truncated before the end, so the final writes are not fully recovered.

name: init_audio_channels_and_buffers
description: Fills a sample buffer with values from a shift-and-XOR generator, then sets the pointers, periods and volumes of the four Amiga audio channels to fixed values. It clears a block of globals and calls a helper.

name: set_channel_control_word
description: For inputs below 99, looks up a channel block from a 26-byte table record and writes a masked control word into it. When bit 14 of the second input is clear it also stores the first input.

name: set_channel_control_word
description: For inputs below 99, looks up a channel block from a 26-byte table record and writes a masked control word into it. When bit 14 of the second input is clear it also stores the first input.

name: set_channel_control_word
description: For inputs below 99, looks up a channel block from a 26-byte table record and writes a masked control word into it. When bit 14 of the second input is clear it also stores the first input.

name: control_audio_dma_channels
description: The shown pseudo-code is a small channel-control routine that does not match this 298-instruction body, so only the listed facts are reliable. They show writes to the Amiga audio channel registers and the DMA control register, where a set bit 15 enables DMA channels, and calls to 21 routines.

name: run_helper_sequence_with_flag
description: Calls a long run of helper routines, branching on a global flag, sets the global to 255, and then calls a final helper.

name: copy_header_and_call_handler
description: If the output pointer is not null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in the data block into it. It then calls the routine held in the address register.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:-AGGRESSORS-:0:0000
name: parse_startup_arguments_and_run
description: Checks whether the program was started from the command line or from Workbench. From the command line it trims the argument text, splits it into words, handles quoted strings with star escapes for newline and escape characters, and calls a routine with the argument count and buffer. From Workbench it replies to the startup message and closes the libraries it opened.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:-AGGRESSORS-:0:01D8
name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library function vectors through the base register at fixed negative offsets and returns, with no other logic.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:-AGGRESSORS-:0:01EA
name: open_library_or_fail
description: Calls a library vector to open a library and returns its base when that succeeds. Otherwise it runs a cleanup sequence of library calls and returns the fixed value 100.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:-AGGRESSORS-:2:0000
name: wait_for_alloc_vector_release
description: Hooks the memory allocation vectors and repeatedly delays while checking whether they are still in use. If another hook remains, it reports in a console window that the program cannot exit while the allocation vector is in use, then tries again.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:-AGGRESSORS-:4:0000
name: call_stored_handler_pointer
description: Calls the routine whose address is held in a global pointer variable, through an indirect call the decompiler could not resolve to a jump table, then returns.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:-AGGRESSORS-:4:000C
name: call_second_stored_handler
description: Calls the routine whose address is held in a second global pointer variable, then returns.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:0:0000
name: run_setpatch_entry_point
description: Program entry: allocates a control block and returns error code 20 if that fails. Otherwise it opens dos.library and either parses the command-line text into arguments or takes the Workbench startup message, calls a routine, closes the libraries, and frees the block.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:0:01A0
name: release_control_block_and_return
description: Stores the given value in the control block, closes the file handle and library when they are set, frees the block, and returns the stored value.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:3:0000
name: call_guarded_pass_through
description: Calls a routine, then if a global flag is nonzero calls a second routine with the parameter and passes its result to a third. It finally calls one more routine.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:3:0030
name: apply_setpatch_patches
description: Records a flag from its parameter, checks the command-line arguments for a usage message and the RAD option, and then patches the Exec, layers.library and trackdisk vectors as the code finds them. Each step is reported with the text messages it references.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:15:0004
name: call_stored_library_routine
description: Calls the routine at offset 46 of the library base held in a global, and returns the value left in the data register.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:8:0000
name: allocate_stub_and_checksum
description: If the memory checks pass and a suitable block can be allocated, copies a short code stub from a neighbouring routine into it and stores its address in the control structure. It then writes the complement of a 16-bit sum over a short word array into a structure field, and returns zero; otherwise it returns 20.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:8:00B4
name: store_checksum_and_call
description: Stores the complement of a 16-bit sum over a short word array in a structure field, then calls the routine through a pointer. The pointer is first adjusted by a fixed amount when a marker word matches, and the jump-table target is not recovered.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:13:0000
name: disable_interrupts_around_patch_calls
description: Opens the disk resource through a library vector and, when that succeeds and a size field is small, disables interrupts by writing the interrupt-enable register and incrementing a nesting byte. It calls two routines through a table, stores their results in two globals, then decrements the byte and re-enables interrupts when it reaches zero.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:13:007C
name: copy_long_on_nonzero_result
description: Calls the routine stored in a global pointer and, when it returns a nonzero value, copies a longword from a fixed offset of the global structure into a global.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:13:0094
name: call_handler_unless_value_matches
description: Returns without action when the stored longword matches the value at a fixed offset in the global structure and is not minus one. Otherwise it calls the routine stored in a second global pointer.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:13:00A8
name: call_handler_if_input_minus_one
description: Returns when the data register input is not minus one. Otherwise it calls the routine stored in the second global pointer.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:5:0000
name: install_marker_and_vector_once
description: Disables interrupts through the interrupt-enable register. When a four-letter marker is not yet present in low memory, it writes the marker and a value there and calls a routine from a table; otherwise it calls a second table routine.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:5:0042
name: call_vector_at_offset_136
description: Calls the routine at offset 136 of the pointer held in a global, then returns.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:9:0000
name: fill_vector_table_from_routine
description: Stores a computed offset in a global, then fills a sixteen-entry longword table at a fixed low-memory location with addresses that step through a routine, two bytes apart.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:9:0038
name: call_helper_repeatedly_return
description: Calls a helper repeatedly in a straight line and returns the result of its last call.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:9:003C
name: call_helper_repeatedly_return
description: Calls a helper repeatedly in a straight line and returns the result of its last call.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:9:003E
name: call_helper_repeatedly_return
description: Calls a helper repeatedly in a straight line and returns the result of its last call.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:9:005E
name: return_input_value
description: Returns the data register input unchanged and performs no other operation.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:7:0000
name: set_function_if_index_small
description: When the word at offset 20 is 35 or less, calls the SetFunction library vector through the exec base. Otherwise it returns without action.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:7:001E
name: allocate_entry_list_or_free
description: Allocates a block with the memory allocator, then fills its entries from the input structure, allocating a further block for each nonzero size word. If an allocation fails it frees the blocks already made and returns a flagged zero; otherwise it returns the block.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:7:0080
name: free_count_blocks_return_flag
description: Calls the FreeMem library vector once for each counted block plus one final call, then returns the value stored at its argument with the top bit set.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:7:0094
name: free_block_return_flag
description: Calls the FreeMem library vector once, then returns the value stored at its argument with the top bit set.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:6:0010
name: empty_stub_routine
description: Returns immediately without doing any work.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:12:0000
name: call_check_and_notify
description: Passes the longword at offset 68 to the routine held in a global pointer. When that returns nonzero, it calls a second and a third routine through global pointers, passing the value to the third, and returns true.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:10:0000
name: scan_for_marker_word
description: Advances through 16-bit words from the input pointer until one has the value 97 in its high byte, then returns a pointer to that word.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:10:001E
name: advance_by_branch_displacement
description: Decodes a relative displacement from the word at the pointer. A zero low byte selects a 16-bit displacement; otherwise an 8-bit displacement is used, both sign-extended. It returns the pointer advanced by that displacement plus one, in words.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:10:0050
name: compute_offset_from_word
description: Reads a 16-bit value two bytes after the input pointer, halves it and sign-extends the 15-bit result. It returns the input pointer advanced by twice that value plus two.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:10:0076
name: compute_three_global_offsets
description: Walks a chain of helper calls that advance a position by two each step, storing three returned pointers into three globals in turn.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:17:0000
name: call_with_stack_slot_pointer
description: Calls another routine with its two parameters and a pointer to a fixed stack slot, then returns.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:setpatch:16:0000
name: format_into_stack_buffer_and_send
description: Formats its input through the exec formatting library call into a 140-byte stack buffer. It measures the resulting text length by scanning to a null byte and, when the length is nonzero, passes the buffer and length to another routine.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:endcli:0:0000
name: size_buffer_from_list_max
description: Finds the maximum of the values in a linked list and uses it to size and fill a buffer. It then copies sixteen longwords into a block and returns zero, or minus one when a step fails.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:endcli:0:0136
name: copy_header_and_call_handler
description: If the output pointer is not null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in the data block into it. It then calls the routine held in the address register.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:DELPHINE:0:0000
name: clear_block_and_dispatch_result
description: Calls a routine, zeroes a large block of longwords starting at a fixed offset from the base register, and stores the base pointer. It calls a library routine when a flag bit is set, then calls a library vector and branches on its result to a fallback or a second routine.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:DELPHINE:0:0006
name: set_global_or_mask_input
description: Returns the input byte ORed with 185 when the overflow and sign flags disagree and the carry is set. Otherwise it stores 32879 in a global and returns the input unchanged.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:DELPHINE:0:0016
name: set_global_bit_one
description: Sets bit 1 of the global and returns. The listed CIAA port register is not accessed in this short body.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:DELPHINE:0:0020
name: build_status_bits_from_global
description: Builds a two-bit status value from the global: bit 0 is set when bit 6 of the global is clear, and bit 1 is set when bit 2 of the global is clear. The listed hardware reads are not in this body.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:DELPHINE:0:0074
name: set_global_constant_79
description: Stores the constant 79 in a global and returns.

key: future wars - time travellers (1989)(u. s. gold)(it)[cr aggressors](disk 1 of 2)/Future Wars - Time Travellers (1989)(U. S. Gold)(It)[cr Aggressors](Disk 1 of 2).adf:DELPHINE:0:007E
name: set_global_to_marker_value
description: Stores the constant 32879 in a global and returns.
